findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing code reuse under concurrent logins
findings.body: The code reads and decrypts the complete backup-code list, validates a code, and then writes a modified copy without any conditional update, transaction isolation, or version check. Two concurrent credential requests using the same code can both read the pre-consumption list and both authenticate successfully; requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's update and restore a previously consumed code. This violates the advertised one-time-use property of backup codes and can result in multiple successful sessions from a single stolen code. Consume the code with an atomic/optimistic conditional update (or store individually hashed codes with a uniqueness/consumption state) and reject a request whose stored state changed before its update.

findings.title: The new backup-code authentication and one-time-use behavior is not tested
findings.body: The added tests only exercise displaying the backup-code screen and downloading/copying its UI. They never authenticate with a generated backup code, verify that a valid code works, verify rejection of an invalid code, or verify that a successfully used code cannot be reused; disabling 2FA with a backup code is also untested. These are the core security-sensitive paths introduced by this PR, so regressions such as failing backup login or non-consuming codes will ship undetected.
